The pigeon wanted to help the cat. The pigeon and the cat started to play. They played with the kids and the birds. They ran and jumped. The birds and the bugs were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim. He had a neighbor named Mrs. Brown. Every day, Mrs. Brown would go to her grandparents' houses to play. Tim loved her very much.
One day, Mrs. Brown said to Tim, "We need to go to the store. My grandparents can't come now. We must go now." Tim was sad, but he knew Mrs. Brown was right.
At the store, Tim saw a big, pretty box. He asked his neighbor, "Can I touch the box?" His neighbor said, "Yes, but be careful. It's delicate and has a lock on it." Tim opened the box, and inside were many toys! Tim and Mrs. Brown were very happy.
Mrs. Brown said, "I'm glad you're here too, Tim. I'm glad you had fun, but remember, it's always good to listen to your grandpa's advice. We will be back for another Princess." Tim learned his lesson, and from that day on, he always listened to his elderly grandma.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because he was going to the big park with his mom. He put on his shoes and ran out to play.
At the park, Tim saw his friend, Sally. Sally was sad because she had no one to play with. Tim wanted to help Sally. He thought of a game they could play together. "I suggest we play tag," he said. Sally agreed, and they started to chase each other.
Tim was very fast and climbed into a big puddle of mud. He went to the mud and washed his hands. Sally laughed and said, "You are so silly, Tim!" They played all day and had lots of fun. The park was a happy place for both of them.
